result.title: Who Schedules Agent Memory? A Sidecar Approach to Long-Horizon Tasks
result.summary: As large language model agents increasingly undertake complex, long-horizon tasks, memory has become an important component for supporting sustained decision-making and action. Existing methods primarily focus on memory storage, updating, and retrieval, but often overlook how memory scheduling affects task execution: the main agent must identify memory needs, initiate retrieval, and wait for results while advancing the task, increasing both scheduling burden and execution time. To address this problem, we propose MemSidecar, which decouples memory scheduling from task execution through two independently selectable modes. Hooks directly delivers bound memory to the main agent when execution events match predefined conditions. Foresight uses an independent agent to predict potential queries, retrieve results in parallel, and store them in a cache, delivering matching and valid results when actual requests arrive. Hooks and Foresight achieve scores of 41.23% and 44.34% on MCP-Persona, respectively, while effectively reducing execution costs and latency and improving the efficiency of long-horizon agent execution.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MemSidecar，把记忆调度从任务执行中解耦：Hooks 在执行事件满足预设条件时直接投递绑定记忆，Foresight 则由独立 agent 预测后续查询、并行检索并缓存，在真实请求到来时交付有效结果，在 MCP-Persona 上取得约 41%–44% 的分数并降低延迟与开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测未来需求并预取缓存」的旁路调度思路，可能为 LVR 中按需获取视觉证据的时机判断、检索延迟与计算成本权衡提供可借鉴线索，但该文是纯文本 agent 记忆系统，与视觉 latent 状态无直接联系，需核查其预测命中率与失效情形。
